newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hispanic populaton growing, Census bureau says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hispanic populaton growing, Census bureau says.

text.p: Hispanics are the fastest growing group of Americans but overall population growth is slowing down, the U.S. Census Bureau said on Saturday.

"We're seeing a slow down, and the lower number of births are being driven by the fact that the baby boomers are really starting to move out of the child bearing ages," said Census spokesman Kevin Deardorff.

Half the U.S. population is over 35, while the other half is under that age. Non-hispanic whites represent the oldest segment of the population with a median age of 37, the bureau said. The median age for non-hispanic blacks is 30, while the median age for hispanics of all races is 26.

Due to their youth, the birth rate among hispanics is the highest of any population group in the country, the bureau said. In 1996, there was a net addition of one million hispanics, while the non-hispanic white population, the largest of any of the racial groups, grew by 600,000 last year, the bureau said.

Nearly 29 million Americans are of hispanic origin, while 194 million are non-hispanic white, the bureau said. African Americans numbered nearly 32 million last year, while there were nearly 10 million Asians, the bureau said. There were about two million American Indians, according to the data.

The latest census data also reflected the baby boom generation moving into middle age. The number of Americans aged 45 to 64 years was 54 million last year, compared to 46 million in 1990, the bureau said.

School-age children numbered nearly 50 million last year, compared with 45 million in 1990, the bureau said. The 65 and older group totalled nearly 34 million last year, compared to 31 million in 1990, the bureau said.

But Deardorff said that number was influenced by a drop in birth rates during the economic depression of the 1930's. He said the latest data showed a sharp increase in the number of Americans 85 years and older.
